title: Marguerite and the Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Harrow's End founder Nathaniel Voss is exhumed for a sesquicentennial ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Ada Thackeray realizes her anonymous tipster 'Marguerite'—who has fed her three solved cold cases—is connected to a disappearance the town buried in 1974. As Ada follows Marguerite's clues through sealed hospital records and a drowned quarry, she discovers Marguerite is Voss's presumed-dead daughter, living hidden under another identity while the town's founding families covered up what really happened the night she vanished. The climax forces Ada to choose between exposing the truth and protecting Marguerite from the last living conspirator, who will kill to keep the grave empty; Ada broadcasts the confession, Marguerite surrenders on her own terms, and justice arrives outside the law that failed her.
about_author: M. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering unsolved cases across New England before turning to fiction. Hartwell lives off-grid in Vermont with two dogs and an unhealthy archive of coroner's reports.

chapters.title: The Empty Suit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the morning of Harrow's End's sesquicentennial, workers lift Nathaniel Voss's coffin for public display and find it filled with river stones and a 1974 hospital gown. Ada, attending anonymously to record ambiance for her podcast, recognizes the gown's tag as matching evidence from a case Marguerite tipped her about. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback-structured. She reviews how Marguerite's anonymous letters led her to solve three deaths ruled accidental—a fall, a fire, a drowning—each quietly corrected without credit. Now the pattern terrifies her: all three victims were connected to Voss's estate. Beat: the cost of being right.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Silent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her dead-drop mailbox at the old rail depot holds no letter, only a single pressed violet—the first non-verbal message in four years. When she asks around town about the exhumation, longtime residents go strangely polite and closed. Beat: isolation tightening.

chapters.title: The Sesquicentennial Speech
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mayor Corinne Ashford. At the ceremony, Corinne smooths over the empty coffin as 'relocation during cemetery maintenance,' but her hands shake reading the founder's biography. She privately burns a box of documents that night. Beat: guilt performing as grace.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the gown tag to shuttered St. Ambrose Sanatorium records, Ada learns a girl named Marguerite Voss was declared dead in 1974—body never recovered from Blackpool Quarry. The witness everyone swears is dead may be alive. Beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: What the Diver Saw
chapters.summary: POV: Ezra Dunn, retired police diver, dying of emphysema. He confesses to his nurse that he searched the quarry in '74 and found nothing—because he was ordered to search the wrong cove. He mails Ada a hand-drawn map before losing his nerve. Beat: cowardice seeking absolution.

chapters.title: The Wrong Cove
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Using Ezra's map, Ada dives the correct cove and finds a rusted satchel containing a child's locket and a ledger of payments from Voss Industries to five town families. Someone watches her from the treeline. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Five Families
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She traces the ledger signatures: the Ashfords, the Merricks, the Boyles, the Fenwicks—and one name scratched out. Three of the family lines still dominate Harrow's End. Her podcast producer warns her the episodes are being quietly demonetized. Beat: the town closing ranks.

chapters.title: A Woman Named Gray
chapters.summary: POV: Ruth Gray, librarian, 71. Ruth recognizes Ada's questions for what they are and, after forty years of silence, leaves a note in a returned book: 'Ask me about the fire.' Beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Fire at Fenwick Hall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ruth tells her about the 1975 fire that killed housekeeper Alma Boyle—the first 'accident'—and admits she saw Alma alive hours after the blaze, fleeing toward the state line with a teenage girl. Beat: grief and awe at ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Demonetized
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her hosting platform suspends the podcast citing 'unverified claims'; a lawyer representing Voss Industries sends a cease-and-desist. Ada realizes someone inside the town government is feeding her movements to the families. Beat: professional annihilation.

chapters.title: Corinne's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: POV: Mayor Corinne Ashford. Cornered by her brother-in-law Douglas Merrick, who reminds her what the ledger means for her children, Corinne nearly goes to Ada but instead hands over her father's old key ring instead of the truth. Beat: complicity inherited, not chosen.

chapters.title: The Key Ring
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. One key fits a forgotten sub-basement beneath the Voss mausoleum, where Ada finds decades of correspondence—including letters signed 'M' addressed to her long-dead mother, revealing Ada's own family received ledger money. Beat: identity shattered; she was never outside this story.

chapters.title: My Mother's Signature
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, raw and confessional. Digging into her late mother's papers, Ada finds her mother co-signed the 1974 hush agreement at nineteen, pregnant and paid off. The realization reframes every 'coincidence' that led Ada to true crime. Beat: betrayal by blood.

chapters.title: Violet Season
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite (as 'Edith Marsh,' schoolteacher). Living under her assumed name for fifty years, Marguerite decides the empty coffin has ended her hiding; she writes one final letter to Ada and plants violets on Alma Boyle's unmarked grave. Beat: resignation becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Dead-Drop Meeting
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the rail depot, Ada finally meets Marguerite—an elegant, wary woman of sixty-five—who explains the night of 1974: she witnessed her father's death at the hands of the five families' patriarchs and fled; they declared her dead to bury the witness. Beat: two lifetimes of silence meeting.

chapters.title: Douglas Merrick's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Douglas Merrick. The last living conspirator's heir calculates exposure—Ezra's map, Ruth's testimony, the ledger—and decides Marguerite must die properly this time. He hires a man to follow Edith Marsh home. Beat: banality of evil, ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: The Man at the Schoolhouse
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada spots the tail outside Marguerite's school and creates a diversion that gets them both out, but the escape exposes Marguerite's address. In a safehouse, Marguerite asks Ada to let it go—for both their mothers' sake. Beat: loyalty versus truth made literal.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Refusing to stay invisible any longer, Ada records a final episode with Marguerite's full testimony, Ezra's map, and the ledger scans, distributing it through independent channels minutes before the takedown lands. Beat: the point of no return, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Blackpool Quarry, Again
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Ada/Marguerite POV. Merrick confronts them at the quarry where it began, intending a double drowning; Corinne arrives having finally chosen truth, recording everything on her phone as Ezra's old dive partner restrains Merrick until state police—alerted by the broadcast—arrive. Beat: justice seized, not granted.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Months later, Nathaniel Voss's real remains are recovered from the mausoleum floor where the patriarchs hid him; Marguerite testifies under her own name, and the three 'accidents' are formally reopened. Ada publishes under her byline for the first time. Beat: grief transmuted into record.

chapters.title: The Pressed Violet
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. At Alma Boyle's new headstone, Marguerite gives Ada a pressed violet like the ones that started everything, and the two women agree the podcast ends here—or perhaps begins, retold honestly. Ada signs off her final episode: 'Some witnesses stay dead so the truth can live.' Beat: peace earned, identity reclaimed.
